component.name: PkgDeck
component.summary: All your package managers in one app

description.p: Search, install, update, and clean up software from every package manager on your computer. PkgDeck works with APT, Flatpak, Snap, Homebrew, developer tools, container images, and firmware updates, and includes the pkd command-line tool.
One cleanup task that changed no longer stops the others.

ul.li: If a task changed since you reviewed it, only that task is skipped and the rest are cleaned
Podman and Docker cleanups still run when an image, volume or container came into use, and keep what is in use
Automatic updates skip only the sources that can't run on their own, not the whole batch
Select all no longer checks cleanups that start unchecked, such as unused volumes and sccache
npm and pnpm installed with fnm, Volta or nvm are found again
Homebrew cleanup still runs when a file it lists changed size
Errors read more clearly, and Activity shows each reason once

description.p: Updates from different sources run at the same time, and pacman updates work on Arch again.

ul.li: APT, Flatpak, Snap and other sources update side by side, with one password per batch
The progress card names every update that is running
Selected pacman updates run in one transaction, with the packages that need their exact version
The window opens at the size you left it, maximized if it was
Screen readers read out the progress card
zypper and DNF no longer show as failed when their first check after a change is slow

description.p: Flatpak update checks no longer fail on apps from bundles or local builds.

ul.li: Apps installed from a .flatpak bundle or a local build are left out of update checks
A source that fails more than once shows once, with every reason
An opened AppImage file can launch without installing it

description.p: The AppImage works on more Linux systems, and Flatpak apps opened from a link can start.

ul.li: The AppImage and Snap start on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 and other systems with glibc 2.39 or newer
A Flatpak link's page shows the app as installed after installing it for the whole system
Installed Flatpak apps opened from a link or file have Launch
Flatpak links remember whether you last installed for yourself or the whole system

description.p: Choose what automatic updates wait for.

ul.li: Automatic updates and cleaning can run on battery
Automatic updates can run on a metered connection
Automatic cleaning no longer waits for a metered connection

description.p: Better pages for opened Flatpak links.

ul.li: A Flatpak link shows the app's icon, description and screenshots when its repository is set up
A Flatpak link for an app installed for all users offers Update or Reinstall instead of Install
A Flatpak link shows the version it installs instead of its branch
App descriptions keep their paragraphs and show list items one per line
Every section and running change words what it's doing the same way
The tray icon can show always, only with updates, or never
Checks can notify, install updates, or do nothing with them
Automatic updates install only from the sources you pick, and wait on metered connections

description.p: Fixes for opened files, Homebrew Casks and KDE.

ul.li: An opened file for something already installed offers Update, or for Flatpak, Reinstall or Downgrade, instead of Install
Going to another page leaves an opened file's page
Flatpak links open in PkgDeck on KDE
Homebrew Casks searches no longer fail on casks with no version for this system
Header buttons drop their labels before covering the page title
